newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up as Central Bank sells dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up as Central Bank sells dlrs.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed slightly firmer at 26.335 to the dollar from Friday's 26.349 as the Central Bank sold dollars to mop up pesos, traders said.
The Central Bank initially posted its selling price at 26.35 at the opening, but adjusted it downward to 26.344 and further down to 26.340 at the close of the session.
"I think the Central Bank was mopping up the pesos from the system. We're swamped with pesos," one trader said.
The Central Bank raised its special Treasury bill rates late last week to siphon off liquidity, but it did not succeed as the T-bill rates remained sideways in today's auction.
The benchmark 91-day T-bill rate just inched up by a mere two basis points. One trader estimated the Central Bank sold about 80 percent of the day's turnover of $141.30 million.
Another trader attributed the peso recovery to the onslaught of foreign funds into the stock market. The bourse closed at another record high on Monday due to strong corporate earnings.
